neighbours.label: the end of a narrative clause reporting a character's doubt, distrust or unimpressed reaction (she was unimpressed. / doesn't trust James,); the same narrative with a trusting or pleased reaction, or a question, stays low
fire: Tom listened to the excuse in silence. He didn't believe a word of it. Then he turned away.
Lena looked at the painting for a long time. She was not impressed. "Is that all?" she asked.
Marcus doesn't trust his new partner, but he needs the money too badly to quit.
The old man read the letter twice. He was thoroughly unconvinced. Outside, the rain kept falling.
When the boy promised to pay her back, Rosa was sceptical. She had heard it all before.
Ellen watched the salesman demonstrate the blender. She remained doubtful. It looked cheap.
Jake had heard the rumour from his cousin. He was suspicious of it, and said so at dinner.
The captain studied the map they had bought. He was utterly bewildered. Nothing matched the coast.
quiet: Tom listened to the plan in silence. He liked every word of it. Then he turned away.
Lena looked at the painting for a long time. She was moved. Is that a real Vermeer?
Marcus admires his new partner, and he plans to stay with the firm for years.
The old man read the letter twice. He was very pleased. Outside, the rain kept falling.
When the boy promised to pay her back, Rosa smiled warmly and gave him the money.
Ellen watched the salesman demonstrate the blender. She bought two. It looked solid.
Jake had heard the news from his cousin. He was happy about it, and said so at dinner.
The captain studied the map they had bought. He nodded with approval. Everything matched the coast.

short: clause end after a character's doubtful/unimpressed reaction
notes: Card peaks are clause-final punctuation in fiction: 'She was unimpressed.', 'Abby doesn't trust James,', 'Bet was completely mystified', 'merely excuses for his abrupt departure.', '"Very true," said Henry'.
